subject: Dedicated capacity plan: recommended GPU SKU mix and tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Shepard <alex.shepard@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity plan: recommended GPU SKU mix and tradeoffs

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — really excited about the opportunity to run your inference workloads on a Redwood Dedicated pool. Attached is a first-pass capacity estimate and a short breakdown of SKU tradeoffs (H100, A100, L4) based on the model families you described. High-level notes up front: 

- Goal: Stay within your latency SLOs (95th < 250ms for interactive queries) while minimizing monthly committed cost.
- Recommendation approach: pick a small H100 pool for large-context, memory-heavy 70B models + a larger A100 pool for general-purpose serving; add L4 nodes for embeddings/bulk inference and cheap asynchronous jobs.

See the attached capacity_estimate_nimbus_v2.xlsx for a scenario matrix (expected qps, avg seq len, batching assumptions). A few quick bullets pulled from the sheet:

- H100 (80GB): recommended for 70B models and any kept warm long-sequence chats — allows larger KV cache, avoids offloading. Use 8–12 GPUs to support canary + steady traffic for the initial phase.
- A100 (40GB): sweet spot for 13B–34B models when you need predictable throughput; good cost/perf for batched, high-concurrency traffic.
- L4 (24GB): very cost-effective for 7B/quantized variants and embeddings; lower per-hour cost but lower single-stream tail performance — use as a scale-out tier.

Questions I want to confirm so we can finalize numbers: typical peak qps per endpoint, expected percent of 70B traffic, and desired canary windows. Once confirmed we can convert the estimate into an MRC commitment and a canary run plan.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm traffic split and any hard latency SLOs by EOD Thursday.
2) We provision a small canary: 2 H100, 4 A100, 6 L4 for 2 weeks to validate tails and cost.
3) We review telemetry together and lock in the committed pool size for month 1.

Attaching: capacity_estimate_nimbus_v2.xlsx and a quick chart (gpu_mixture_chart.png).

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the detailed breakdown and the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock anything down: 

1) Memory headroom: our clinical summarization pipeline sometimes uses ~32k tokens for long patient histories. Which SKU do you expect will reliably hold a 32k sequence without offload/latency spikes?
2) Cost / unit economics: can you give an example monthly committed cost for the 2/4/6 canary you suggested vs a steady-state 12/24/48 mix so our procurement team has something concrete to evaluate?
3) Failover behavior: if H100 pool is saturated, can we automatically route a subset of traffic to quantized A100 or L4 variants with graceful degradation?

procurement@nimbushealth.com — looping you in so procurement has the ballpark numbers and can flag any compliance/PO constraints early.

Thanks,

On Mon, Jun 14, 2026 at 12:05 PM Alex Shepard <alex.shepard@nimbushealth.com> wrote:
> Marissa — thanks for the detailed breakdown and the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock anything down: 
> 
> 1) Memory headroom: our clinical summarization pipeline sometimes uses ~32k tokens for long patient histories. Which SKU do you expect will reliably hold a 32k sequence without offload/latency spikes?

Hi Alex — quick notes from infra/serving:

- For 32k tokens and heavy KV cache needs, H100 80GB is the reliable choice out-of-the-box. It avoids frequent NVMe offload for the KV cache and keeps tail latency predictable.
- A100 80GB (if available in the customer's region) can also work for some models, but A100 40GB will be tight for 32k unless you quantize aggressively and accept some offload behavior.
- L4s are not suitable for sustained 32k interactive sessions; they're fine for embeddings and short-turn inference.

On failover and routing: we have smart-routing policies that can do graceful degradation — e.g., route non-critical eleborations to a quantized variant on A100/L4 while keeping the primary H100 pool for core interactive traffic. This can be automated with canary percentages and SLA thresholds.

On cost modeling: attached is the sheet Marissa shared. For quick ballpark numbers (all monthly committed):
- Canary (2 H100 / 4 A100 / 6 L4): estimated committed spend ~$68k/mo, expected blended latency under target for 80% of traffic, with 95th tail monitored during canary.
- Steady-state conservative (12 H100 / 24 A100 / 48 L4): estimated committed spend ~$520k/mo, yields headroom for 2–3x peak and removes most queuing.
- Aggressive quantized option (replace half A100 with L4 for non-critical traffic): ~25–30% lower monthly spend but expect higher 95th for complex sequences.

We'll also instrument KV cache warmers and per-route batching to reduce per-token cost; those optimizations typically cut GPU time by ~15–30% depending on workload.

Vivek — any comments on SLA wording we should surface to procurement?

— Dev

Alex / procurement team — thanks for the quick review. Summarizing the agreed plan and next steps so we can put something into DocuSign: 

1) Canary provisioning (2 H100 80GB, 4 A100 40GB, 6 L4 24GB) for 14 days to validate tails and cost. Redwood will enable smart-routing and set up telemetry dashboards.
2) If canary metrics meet latency and error-rate thresholds (documented in the sheet), we convert to a 3-month committed pool: target 10 H100 / 20 A100 / 40 L4. Exact numbers will be finalized after canary.
3) Failover: we will configure automatic traffic shaping that routes overflow to quantized A100/L4 variants with a configurable degradation policy; full details to be in the SOW addendum.
